correctness.rationale: Independently reduced the spin generator to the centered, bias-normalized fermionic one-particle matrix M. Its equation has commutator with hopping 2 and centered diagonal U(3,1,−1,−3), damping (G/2){B,M} at the endpoints B=diag(1,0,0,1), damping 2γ on the off-diagonal, and drive diag(G,0,0,−G). The current divided by f is 4 Im M_12. The dissipative part of the homogeneous equation forces zero boundary rows and columns by the real Hilbert–Schmidt pairing; the commutator and nonzero hopping force the remaining rows to vanish even at γ=0. Reflection with alternating site signs and conjugation reduce the system to ten real unknowns. Exact elimination reproduced both zero-dephasing rational formulas, the six polynomial coefficients and all thirteen derivative coefficients at G=1. See `python /workspace/branches/review-computations/check_transport.py`; frozen code was inspected, not executed. The positive W coefficients yield a simple unique threshold. Under W=xG² at small G or W=x/G² at large G, scaled polynomials tend respectively to 2293760x−49152 and x−192; bracket their roots to justify both laws. At G=1 the ordered root brackets imply either strict negativity on γ>0 or exactly one positive zero of the derivative with a positive-to-negative crossing. At scale γ=cU, the leading denominator is nonzero for c>0, so the leading quotient and its c derivative converge uniformly near c=1. Bracketing by c on either side of 1 gives the optimizer and current limits. All-G checks are only initial-response checks for the frozen result.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The limiting derivative has opposite signs at fixed c values below and above 1. The already-proved unique resistance minimum then brackets g*/U→1, and the compact-uniform resistance limit gives UI_4/f→4/3. The source need not print those numerical limits for the implication to hold. Jacob et al.'s approximate large-chain γ_max≈U/ℏ is not itself an exact four-site result.
